With unit-normal width normalized to two, the exact feasible triple polytope has six enumerated vertices and the rigorously bounded strictly convex quadratic reaches its maximum only at two extremal triples. Equality in the positive/negative mass inequalities proves every minimizing normal and excludes all others even at the tie. Squared diameters follow by exact within/cross vertex-pair maximization. An independently replayable finite rational checker checks 54 profiles and 82,080 normals; infinite quantifiers rely on the proof, not samples.

value.rationale: These two Ehrhart-equivalent canonical polytopes are a well-motivated test of how lattice equivalence fails to control Euclidean geometry. The result determines two distinct sharp phase boundaries, one governed only by anisotropy in the complete minimizing-normal set and one by both level sizes and anisotropy in the farthest-pair structure, with exact extremizers. In unscaled geometry, the positive gap in minimal width is independent of dimension. These statements characterize a natural infinite family rather than arbitrary samples or a routine numerical improvement.
